newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher on moderate volumes.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher on moderate volumes.

text.p: COMEX copper futures ended higher Friday, on moderate volumes, with the backwardations firm also.
"Copper prices popped up on the opening after the drop in LME stocks but did little for the rest of the day," one trader said.
"There was continuing interest in arbitrage business but as everybody wanted to do the same thing, not much business got done."

LME copper stocks fell 4,275 tonnes to 201,250 tonnes Friday, slightly more than expected, while COMEX copper stocks rose 1,744 short tons Thursday to 31,861 short tons and were up 713 short tons Friday to 32,574 short tons.
The COMEX/LME arbitrage of nearly 5.00 cents a pound in the front month is seen responsible for attracting inventories to COMEX warehouses from LME, traders said.
COMEX May copper ended up 1.85 cents at 110.95 cents a pound, after trading a 108.90-111.40 range.
After finding support around 108.00 cents on intraday hourly charts, and taking out resistance around 110.50 cents, the rally may now resume, technical analysts said.
Daily momentum oscillators show room for more upside next week though, with five-day slow stochastic recovering from around 20 pct and nine-day RSI recovering from neutral zone around 50 pct.
COMEX May/July spread widened to 3.65 cents a pound intraday before ending steady around 3.30 cents.
COMEX and LME copper prices reached an eight month high last week, driven by seasonal demand and a tight prompt market.
